title: Enterprise onboarding - Health checks, QBRs, Integration & Escalation playbook
author: Avery Chen
body:
Summary

This playbook consolidates the canonical steps, owners, and artifacts for enterprise customer onboarding at Redwood Inference, with a focus on recurring health checks, QBR (Quarterly Business Review) materials, integration guidance, escalation routing, and a curated list of known issues and workarounds. This document is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and on-call SREs who participate in initial and ongoing enterprise customer health activities.

Scope

- Applies to customers on Dedicated and Private deployments and high-touch Hosted accounts (monthly committed spend > $15k).
- Covers onboarding through first 3 QBRs (~9 months), ongoing health checks, and documented escalation paths for production-impacting issues.
- Does not replace runbooks owned by Eng-SRE or Eng-Serving-Runtime; instead it references them.

Key Objectives

1. Reduce time-to-first-successful-inference (TTFSI) for enterprise customers to <= 10 business days from contract signature for standard integrations.
2. Maintain a documented weekly health cadence during the first 90 days and a QBR cadence thereafter.
3. Ensure a clear escalation path with max time-to-response targets: P1 initial response < 1 hour, resolution/mitigation plan within 4 hours.

Roles and ownership

- Customer Success Manager (CSM): primary onboarding coordinator, owns QBR content and customer success plan.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical lead for integration, initial validation, authentication, and performance tuning.
- Support Engineer (L2): triage and operational support for incidents and known issues.
- Eng-SRE (L3): escalation target for production incidents and platform-level degradations.
- Account Executive (AE): commercial owner for contractual updates and upsell conversations.

Onboarding checklist (90-day milestone-driven)

Stage 0 - Pre-kickoff (days -7 to 0)
- Deliver welcome packet: API keys, sample prompts, security questionnaire.
- Share onboarding timeline and success metrics (TTFSI, P95 latency, error rate).
- SE prepares test model(s) and token budget for initial validation.

Stage 1 - Kickoff (day 0)
- Attendees: CSM, SE, customer technical lead, security contact.
- Agenda: goals, data flows, network topology, authentication, compliance requirements, acceptance criteria.
- Deliverables: signed integration checklist, designated staging environment.

Stage 2 - Integration & validation (days 1-21)
- SE implements auth (API key, OAuth, or mutual TLS), configures routing policies (region/cost tier), and validates model selection.
- Run perf smoke tests (see 'Performance validation commands' below).
- Complete a security/pen test intake if required by confidentiality level.

Stage 3 - Production onboarding (days 22-60)
- Migrate traffic to production with canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 3-5 business days, monitoring SLOs at each interval.
- Enable recommended caching and batching settings for cost optimization.
- Schedule first 30-day health check.

Stage 4 - Stabilize & QBR readiness (days 60-90)
- Confirm SLO attainment over 30-day window.
- Prepare QBR deck: usage, cost breakdown, latency percentiles, error trends, model quality metrics, and recommended optimizations.
- Transition to regular health cadence and CSM-owned QBR schedule.

Integration guidance (concise)

Authentication and network
- Preferred: API keys + VPC peering for dedicated/private customers. For high-security customers, enable mutual TLS and KMS integration for key management.
- Ensure egress firewall rules allow outbound to the Redwood control plane and specific inference endpoints (list provided during kickoff).

Model selection and performance tradeoffs
- Default recommendation: use curated Redwood-verified model variant matching desired quality/latency tradeoff (e.g., redwood-medium-quantized for production latency-sensitive workloads).
- If cost is primary constraint, enable int8 quantization profile and intelligent batching. SE to run a model-comparison with customer sample prompts.

Performance validation commands (examples)
- Curl smoke test:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-medium","input":"Hello world"}'
- Simple latency measurement (node/python snippet provided in onboarding repo).

Security & compliance checklist

- Confirm data residency or retention requirements; enable data-retention policy in Console.
- Verify KMS/HSM integration if required.
- Confirm audit logging: ensure customer has log access to request IDs, model versions, and request metadata for the agreed retention window.

Health checks cadence and templates

Weekly health checks (first 90 days)
- Owner: CSM + SE.
- Agenda: active rollout status, SLOs (latency/error), request volume, top error signatures, top prompt patterns, action items.
- Deliverable: short health note in CRM (1-2 paragraphs) and updated action list.

30/60/90 day milestone reports
- Owner: CSM.
- Include: adoption metrics, performance summary (P50/P95/P99 latency), cost per 1k tokens, top issues, outstanding action items, plan for next 30 days.

QBR template (quarterly) - slide outline

1. Executive summary: adoption, value realized, roadmap alignment
2. Key metrics: MRR/usage, latency percentiles, error rates, cost breakdown by model and route
3. Reliability: incidents since last QBR, MTTR, mitigations and ownership
4. Feature requests and roadmap asks
5. Optimization opportunities: batching, caching, quantization, model swaps
6. Action plan and owners (next quarter)

Escalation paths and response targets

Priority definitions
- P1 (Production down / critical data loss): customer-facing outage, affinity to business-critical features. Target: initial response < 1 hour, mitigation plan within 4 hours.
- P2 (Degraded critical paths): increased latency > 2x P95 baseline or error rate > 5% for 30+ minutes. Target: initial response < 4 hours, remediation plan within 8 business hours.
- P3 (Non-critical): feature regressions, minor bugs. Target: response < 48 business hours.

Escalation matrix (contacts and channels)
- Step 0: Customer submits ticket via Support portal or opens chat in Console. Support SLA categorizes and acknowledges.
- Step 1: Support L2 triage. If confirmed platform issue or unknown root cause, escalate to Eng-SRE via PagerDuty with incident context and correlation IDs.
- Step 2: Eng-SRE leads incident response and provides customer-facing mitigation steps. CSM coordinates comms and executive updates.
- Step 3: Escalate to Eng-Serving-Runtime and Product VP for cross-team coordination for complex regressions or product-level rollbacks.

Contact table (high-level)

- Support portal: support.redwood.ai (primary intake)
- PagerDuty (Escalations): eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai (pager)
- Customer success urgent contact: csm-oncall@redwood.ai
- Executive escalation: vp-product@redwood.ai (for contractual/regulatory-critical issues)

Known issues and workarounds (curated list)

Note: This is a concise subset; the full canonical list lives in /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/known-issues.

1) Intermittent 502s during high concurrency windows
- Symptoms: short bursts of 502s when client QPS spikes with many long-context requests.
- Impact: request failures, increased retries from clients.
- Workaround: reduce concurrency per-client via client-side throttling and enable workload-aware batching. SEs should enable per-route rate limits and bump canary windows.

2) Increased latency after model rollout to a quantized build
- Symptoms: higher latency P95 due to kernel fallback on some GPU types.
- Impact: degraded perceived performance for customers pinned to that variant.
- Workaround: temporarily rollback to previous variant, or switch to a different quantization profile (medium rather than aggressive). SE to file a kernel compatibility ticket with Eng-Serving-Runtime.

3) Auth failures for VPC/private control plane customers
- Symptoms: 401/403 for requests coming from newly provisioned subnets.
- Impact: requests rejected until network/firewall rules updated.
- Workaround: verify egress DNS and NAT rules, confirm that control-plane endpoints are whitelisted and run the connectivity test script included in onboarding repo.

Support process (ticket lifecycle)

1. Intake: Ticket submitted via support portal or created by SE during onboarding. Support acknowledges within SLA window based on priority.
2. Triage: Support L2 reproduces and gathers logs, request IDs, and minimal reproducer.
3. Escalate: If unresolved, include Eng-SRE and SE with reproduction steps, timeframe, and business impact.
4. Communicate: CSM sends daily updates for P1 until resolved; weekly for P2.
5. Close: Confirm resolution with customer and document root cause and retro in postmortem if P1/P2.

Metrics, SLOs and dashboards to monitor

- SLOs to track during onboarding:
  - Availability: 99.9% (monthly) for production routes
  - Latency: P95 < 350ms (hosted) / P95 < 600ms (dedicated, model dependent)
  - Error rate: < 0.5% (production)

- Dashboards: provide CSM with a QBR dashboard template that includes tokens consumed, average cost per 1k tokens, P50/P95/P99 latency, top error signatures, top prompts by volume.

Templates and attachments (links)

- Onboarding checklist (spreadsheet): /shared/onboarding/checklists/enterprise-onboarding-template.xlsx
- Health check one-pager (editable): /shared/templates/health-check-template.md
- QBR slide deck template: /shared/templates/qbr/redwood-qbr-template.pptx
- Integration test scripts: git repo link provided during kickoff (internal).

Appendix: sample mitigation play for P1 (concise)

1. Acknowledge and open incident ticket (Support L2) within 15 minutes of detection.
2. Add Eng-SRE on call and SE; post short public note to customer channels with ETA.
3. Triage logs and identify last successful request ID. If platform issue, activate failover routing to fallback model/region.
4. If cause is customer config, provide rollback steps and coordinate with customer to revert change.
5. After remediation, schedule a post-incident review and update this playbook if required.

Related runbooks and reference links

- Eng-SRE incident runbooks: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks
- Runtime known issues and kernel tickets: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/known-issues
- Security and compliance onboarding: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging

Revision history

- 2026-10-15: Initial draft by Avery Chen.
- 2026-10-22: Review feedback incorporated from SE and Eng-SRE reviewers.
- 2026-11-01: Finalized QBR template and published.

If you are a CSM/SE preparing a new onboarding, follow the checklist at the top of this doc, attach the filled onboarding spreadsheet, and ping csm-oncall@redwood.ai to schedule the kickoff within 5 business days.
